paper.title_en: Thermodynamics of magnetized asymmetric nuclear matter at finite density and temperature: A chiral model approach
paper.abstract_en: The thermodynamics of an isospin asymmetric dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and magnetic field is studied within the chiral SU(3) model approach. The effective model Lagrangian is based on the non-linear realization of chiral SU(3)L × SU(3)R symmetry and various symmetry breaking effects. Effects of density (ρB), isospin asymmetry (η), temperature (T) and magnetic field (|eB|) are incorporated through the number and scalar densities of nucleons in the self-consistent solutions of meson-field equations. The effects of magnetic field are incorporated through Landau energy levels of protons and anomalous magnetic moments (AMMs) of nucleons along with the magnetized vacuum corrections with finite AMMs of Dirac sea nucleons. Inclusion of the later effect leads to the important phenomenon of inverse magnetic catalysis. A field-induced anisotropy is observed in pressure, isothermal compressibility and squared speed of sound of matter giving rise to different values in the parallel and perpendicular directions with respect to field. The effect of nuclear matter asymmetry gives considerable impact on the various thermodynamic properties of the system. The present study is particularly relevant in the context of highly dense compact star objects e.g., magnetars as well as for the neutron-proton asymmetric matter expected to be produced in heavy-ion collision experiments at CBM, FAIR.
